video_title: What Election Night Means for Markets | Protect the Pile Episode 30
gist: Hedgeye's RPK, Sam and John host chief political strategist JT Taylor days before the 2026 midterms. Taylor forecasts about 53-54 Democratic Senate seats, House gains of 10-12 to the mid-20s, possible election-night delays, a backlash against data centers reshaping races in Ohio, Pennsylvania and Texas, a likely lame-duck omnibus, and a defense topline near $1.15T rather than $1.5T.

insights.claim: Going into month-end October 2026, the S&P 500 was at 7,628, about 2.5% below its all-time high, while the Mag 7 had fallen about 8% over the prior two weeks.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kent (RPK, Hedgeye Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Mega-cap tech is weakening into the election even though the index is near its highs.
insights.quote: uh two and a half percent off the all-time high

insights.claim: JT Taylor's median forecast is that Democrats win about 53-54 Senate seats, with tails from 49 to 56; Kalshi prices Democratic Senate control at 60%+.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: A Democratic Senate would change the odds on legislation and confirmations in 2027.

insights.claim: Taylor ranks Ohio as the likeliest Senate flip because of down-ballot effects from Amy Acton pulling ahead of Vivek Ramaswamy in the governor's race, which helps Sherrod Brown, followed by Texas and Maine.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Ohio is a key bellwether to watch on election night.

insights.claim: Elon Musk has reportedly spent roughly $275-350 million across multiple super PACs, much of it in Texas, and Taylor argues the 'Musk factor' and Ken Paxton's weakness as a candidate could backfire on Republicans while drawing money away from other states.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: A large self-funded effort can turn into a liability when corruption is the dominant issue.

insights.claim: Republicans sat on cash until after Labor Day, and because super PACs pay higher ad rates than candidates, late Republican spending is less efficient and recent reporting suggests it is not working as intended.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Fundraising leads overstate Republicans' real ad reach.

insights.claim: Ticket-splitting has collapsed from about 8-10% of the electorate in 2006 to about 2-3% in 2024, so Democratic wins in states Trump carried by double digits (Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska) require a large shift in sentiment.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Highly polarized electorates make wave results binary and correlated across races.
insights.quote: In 2024, 2 to 3% of the population split their ticket.

insights.claim: Kansas could elect a Democratic senator for the first time since the 1930s because Roger Marshall is weighed down by a medical-billing controversy and very high negatives.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Seeing Kansas in play signals a broad wave.

insights.claim: Taylor sets a floor of about 10-12 House seat gains for Democrats and a ceiling in the mid-20s (from 214 seats today), with the ceiling capped by mid-decade redistricting; the Cook ratings put about 220 seats as solid, likely or lean Democratic.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: A Democratic House is the base case; how large the majority is matters for governing.

insights.claim: Hakeem Jeffries needs about 230+ seats to govern without being held hostage by DSA-aligned members on centrist bills such as defense spending; a gain of 10 seats or fewer could embolden them in the Speaker vote.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: A slim Democratic majority makes House chaos and fiscal deadlock more likely.

insights.claim: Polls show the top voter issues are the economy/affordability, social issues and checks on presidential power, and a Wall Street Journal piece says corruption has overtaken affordability on the campaign trail.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor / Hedgeye panel
insights.so_what: Corruption stories, such as the ambassador to Greece episode, are hurting Republicans late in the campaign.

insights.claim: Results may not be known on election night: Maine and Alaska use ranked-choice voting, one state counts mail ballots for three days, California hand-counts, a close Texas race allows a recount, and challenges to ballots and early or mail voting have been prepared.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: A close result raises the risk of contested-election volatility; a decisive blue night lowers it.

insights.claim: Anti-AI and anti-data-center sentiment is hurting candidates in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Texas and Georgia; Governor Shapiro paused data centers but signaled resumption with conditions, and Greg Abbott flip-flopped on them.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Permitting friction and stricter conditions for data-center build-outs in key states will likely persist after the election.

insights.claim: Ohio has seen more money spent on the data-center issue than any other state, and Sherrod Brown forced Jon Husted to change his position; if Democrats sweep Ohio, they will find it politically hard to reverse anti-data-center rhetoric.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor / Sam
insights.so_what: Ohio is a risk for data-center projects there.

insights.claim: Sam argues that tax revenue and requirements for data centers to pay for their own power or feed power back to the grid make the economic case compelling for either party, while RPK compares the backlash to fracking fears that faded.
insights.speaker: Sam / RPK (Hedgeye Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The political backlash may be louder than the policy actually changes, though the cost of concessions rises.

insights.claim: Taylor and the panel expect that if Congress deadlocks on AI and data-center policy, states will act, and Democrats could control as many as 26 governorships, raising the prospect of 50 different rulebooks.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: A patchwork of state AI regulation is a growing compliance risk.

insights.claim: Taylor sees a better-than-50% chance of an omnibus in the lame duck, with appropriations around the December 11 deadline (possibly with a short CR) and the NDAA, transportation and crypto bills uncertain.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Shutdown risk around December 11 is real but a deal is the base case.

insights.claim: Defense topline is likely to land near the committee baseline of about $1.15 trillion rather than the administration's $1.5 trillion request (versus $980B last year), with an emergency Iran war supplemental of $60-80 billion, more likely at the low end.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Defense budget upside is limited; a supplemental is more likely than a larger topline.

insights.claim: This could be the first year in 65 years without an NDAA.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Defense contractors face funding uncertainty.

insights.claim: Taylor's outlier view is that a Democratic sweep would push Democrats to compromise with Trump on a few issues such as healthcare or energy in 2027, so they have results to show going into 2028.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: The market may be underpricing the chance of limited bipartisan legislation in 2027.
insights.quote: Do not rule out compromise with Trump on probably a handful of issues.

insights.claim: A large Democratic win could make Trump a lame duck with Congress for the first time since 2016, while he would continue his regulatory agenda unabated through executive action.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Expect policy to keep moving through executive and regulatory action rather than legislation.

insights.claim: Defense Secretary Hegseth faces an impeachment push (possibly via discharge petition) and may be the first 'sacrificial lamb' if Republicans lose badly, and the panel speculates he could be traded for a larger defense bill.
insights.speaker: JT Taylor (Hedgeye chief political strategist)
insights.so_what: Expect Pentagon leadership turnover risk after the midterms.
